blocks.text: Murrayville homes listed and sold, June to October 2026

Murrayville, October 2026. Detached houses: 37 listed at month end and 3 sold in October, a sales ratio of 8% (a buyers’ market). Condos and townhomes: 31 listed at month end and 7 sold in October, a sales ratio of 23% (a sellers’ market).

blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Looking across the period, Detached houses: 20 sold over 5 months against an average of 27.4 listed, about 6.8 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was September with 5 sold. Condos and townhomes: 33 sold over 5 months against an average of 31.0 listed, about 4.7 months of listings at that pace; the busiest month was September with 8 sold.

Murrayville sits on both sides of the Fraser Highway immediately east of the City of Langley, inside the Township of Langley.

Its civic core is the Fraser Highway corridor around 216 Street and 222 Street, where Langley Memorial Hospital at 22051 Fraser Highway and W.C. Blair Recreation Centre at 22200 Fraser Highway stand a block apart.
Old Yale Road runs along its south side, with James Hill Elementary at 22144 Old Yale Road on that road.
Murrayville's stock is a mix of detached houses, townhomes and some condos, not a single-form area.
The detached pattern includes older ranchers on larger lots and newer streets, alongside strata townhome complexes on 48A Avenue and 50 Avenue and a low-rise condo form on 221A Street.

The Murrayville Community Plan is Amendment Bylaw 1988 No. 2661 to the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842, adopted April 17, 1989, and amended by the 2025 Official Community Plan Update, Bylaw No. 6200, on December 1, 2025.

Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing (SSMUH) in the Township runs under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 Amendment (SSMUH) Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024: an eligible lot may hold 3 units at 280 square metres or smaller, or 4 units between 280 and 4,050 square metres.

Eligibility is narrow: the lot must be inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on both municipal water and sewer, not heritage-designated and not in a Transit-Oriented Area, and lots over 4,050 square metres are not eligible; there is no 6-unit transit tier in the Township.

blocks.text: Murrayville: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: A secondary suite adds its own utility charges in the Township: for 2026 the flat-rate additions are $233.99 for water and $214.94 for sanitary sewer on top of the house rates.

Metered Township homes are billed three times a year, with meters read in April, August and December, sewer volume charged at 80 percent of water supplied, and a 10 percent penalty on unpaid metered balances after the due date.
Garbage is charged as a $226.00 base rate plus a cart charge for 2026 — $200.00 for a 240-litre cart or $100.00 for a 120-litre cart — and only properties receiving municipal collection pay it.

The Township's 2026 budget raised property taxes 3.97 percent, split as 0.90 percent core services, 1.59 percent RCMP (Royal Canadian Mounted Police), 1.26 percent fire and 0.22 percent bylaw enforcement.

The governing plan itself changed recently: the Murrayville Community Plan consolidation records the 2025 Official Community Plan Update, Amendment Bylaw No. 6200, dated December 1, 2025, which is the plan framework any new Murrayville application is read against.
The 2026 flat-rate utility bill for a Township single-family home is $779.96 for water plus $716.47 for sanitary sewer, before garbage, and utilities are billed separately from property taxes.
Multi-family homes pay less under the split rates adopted for 2026: $667.22 for water and $609.00 for sanitary sewer.
Township property taxes were due July 2, 2026, with 5 percent penalties at midnight July 2 and midnight September 3, 2026.
Fraser Highway is the through route, running east-west through Murrayville toward Aldergrove and Abbotsford and west into Langley City and Surrey.
No SkyTrain or West Coast Express station is in Murrayville; the Surrey-Langley SkyTrain extension now under construction ends at 203 Street in Langley City, west of Murrayville.

Check Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) status and watercourses in the Township's GeoSource viewer before assuming a south or east Murrayville lot can be built on or split, because much Township land is in the ALR.
Check heritage designation before pricing in extra units: a heritage-designated lot is not eligible for Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing under Bylaw No. 6020.

faq.q: How many units can my Murrayville lot hold under the new provincial rules?
faq.a: At most four, and only if the lot qualifies. Under Township Bylaw No. 6020 an eligible lot holds 3 units at 280 square metres or less and 4 units up to 4,050 square metres, provided it is inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on municipal water and sewer, not heritage-designated and not in a Transit-Oriented Area.

faq.q: Is the hospital actually in Murrayville?
faq.a: Yes — it anchors the neighbourhood's civic core. Fraser Health lists Langley Memorial Hospital at 22051 Fraser Highway as a community hospital with 24/7 emergency, general medicine, general surgery and maternity services, and W.C. Blair Recreation Centre at 22200 Fraser Highway is in the same block.
A school's address is not a catchment promise, so confirm the home's address in the School District 35 locator.

faq.q: When are Township taxes due, and what happens if they are late?
faq.a: They were due Thursday, July 2, 2026. The Township applies a 5 percent penalty at midnight July 2, 2026 and a further 5 percent at midnight September 3, 2026, and utility fees are now billed on a separate statement from the tax notice.

faq.q: Is Langley Memorial Hospital in Murrayville?
faq.a: Fraser Health lists Langley Memorial Hospital at 22051 Fraser Highway, Langley, as a community hospital with 24/7 emergency services, open 24 hours a day, 7 days a week; it sits in Murrayville's hospital and civic area

faq.q: How many units can an eligible Murrayville lot hold under SSMUH?
faq.a: Under Township Bylaw No. 6020 (adopted November 18, 2024): 3 units for lots of 280 m² or less and 4 units for lots between 280 m² and 4,050 m², if the lot is inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on municipal water and sewer, not heritage-designated and not in a Transit-Oriented Area; lots over 4,050 m² are not eligible and there is no 6-unit tier in the Township
